The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Jayanagar Sub- Division,
Basavanagudi Police Station, Bengaluru City has filed Police Report against accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2.

The brief case of the Prosecution are as under:-
The complainant in his complaint has alleged that he was running a travel business under the name and style of "New Car Mobile" and he is also having taxi car.
He has purchased the said cars under loan from ICICI Bank, M.G.Road, Bengaluru.
Accused No.2 was working as Vigilance Officer at Vijaya Bank, M.G.Road, Bengaluru was regularly hiring the vehicles to Vijaya Bank since 2010 and he was very much close with the complainant.
Accused No.2 was retired during the year 2011.

Along with accused No.1 accused No.3 came to the office of the complainant and stated that they have started a company in the name and style as "Apex Consultants/Apex Training &
Consultancy Service Pte. Ltd.".

sentences.text: Accused No.2 introduced accused No.1 to the complainant.
Accused No.1 is none other than the son of accused No.2 and addressed him as CEO of the said company.

They further have stated that they are in the process of recruitment of staff and students from various countries for training of the said company and they required multi Volvo buses with chemical toilets.
They have undertaken to pay charges.

Accused No.2 further informed the complainant that the head office of their company by name "Apex Consultants/Apex Training &
Consultancy Service Pte. Ltd." was situated at Singapore and they are having Branch Office at Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the complainant and CEO Accused No1 of the company entered into an Agreement on 21.07.2012 for supply of Volvo buses to the said company in 10 batches for 3 years.
Per day charge was of Rs.25,000/- each bus and the total amount was Rs.1,00,000/-.
The complainant further has alleged that based on the said agreement, he had obtained huge loan from Corporation Bank of Rs.3.19 Crores for the purpose of purchase of 4 Volvo buses.
The Corporation Bank has sanctioned the said loan on hypothecation of 4 Volvo buses on 27.09.2012.
The complainant had informed the accused company about the purchase of the said Volvo buses.
The complainant even had obtained private service vehicle permission from RTO Office.
As per the said private service vehicle permission, the said buses shall be used only to run to the company and it cannot be used for public purpose.
The said buses were purchased by the complainant only for the purpose of the accused company as per Agreement dated 21.07.2012 as well as 07.11.2012.
The accused company has advanced an amount of Rs.19.20 lakhs through cheque.
But, however later the accused has sent his representative by name Srinivas to return back the said cheque and told the complainant that they will pay DD and will inform through e- mail.

sentences.text: The accused persons have collected commission on 03.10.2011 through DD for Rs.3.85 lakhs.
They have also collected Rs.4.50 lakhs as Caution Deposit on 01.03.2012 through cheques.
They have totally collected an amount of Rs.8.35 lakhs from the complainant.
Later, the accused company has issued a cheque to the complainant but it was bounced.
The complainant later verified to ascertain whether the said company was existed at Singapore.
But he was surprised that the said company was not at all existed at Singapore and the accused persons have played fraud and cheated the complainant.
The complainant has suffered huge loss.
On these grounds, the complainant has filed this complaint before this court.
This court by acting U/s 156(3) of Cr.PC referred the matter to the PS for investigation.

4. The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Jayanagar Sub- Division, Basavanagudi Police Station,
Bengaluru City has registered the case in Crime No.12/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
The Investigation officer had recorded the statement of witnesses and conducted panchanama.

After completion of investigation,
he has filed final report against accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
5.

This Court had taken cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465,
467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of IPC and registered a case in register No.III based on the charge sheet, statements of witnesses and documents.

After appearance of accused No.1 and 2, charge sheet copy, statement of witnesses and documents filed with the charge sheet had been supplied to accused No.1 and 2 and provision under Section 207 of Cr.P.C. is complied.

After hearing both sides,
this Court had framed charge against accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
Accused No.1 and 2 have not admitted guilt and claimed to be tried.
6. The Prosecution has examined only one witness as PW.1.
No documents are marked.
The statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C is dispensed with as CW1 informant turned hostile.
7. Heard both sides.
Perused charge, prosecution papers and evidence on record.

8. The points arise for my consideration are as below:
1. Whether Prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable grounds that accused No.1 and 2 have committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465,
467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code ?.
2.
What order or sentence?

9. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following;

3 10. POINT No.1 :- The Prosecution has examined CW.1/PW.1 by name Govindaraju V. who is the complainant in the present case.
This CW1-PW1totally has turned hostile to his own case.
In his evidence he has deposed that the accused No 1 and 2 his buses on monthly rent of Rs.25,000/- and they have issued the cheque of Rs.19.20 lakhs.
The said cheque was bounced but later they have paid the entire settlement amount to the complainant.
The complainant has filed this complaint only on misunderstanding with the accused No. 1 and 2.
The entire due amount from the accused No. 1 and 2 have been received.
There is no further due from the accused No. 1 and 2.
Based on this hostile evidence of PW1, this Court finds that the purpose will not be served in examination of rest of prosecution witnesses.

It looks that the accused No. 1 and 2 and the complainant out of Court have settled their dispute and based on their settlement, the complainant CW1-PW1 has deposed that there is no due from the accused No. 1 and 2.
PW1 in his cross-examination has also stick to his own version and deposed that they have settled their dispute amicably.
When such being the case, this Court finds that there is no evidence to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
11. POINT NO.2:-

In view of the reasons discussed at point No.1 above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDERS Acting Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 471 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Their bail bond and surety bond executed by accused No.1 and 2 will be in force till appeal period.
